title: CPU Pipelining: Overlap and Hazards
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: data hazard — Dependency on unavailable result.
control hazard — Branch uncertainty interrupting fetch.

blocks.title: Observe
blocks.text: Pipelining splits instruction processing into stages; several instructions can occupy different stages during the same clock cycle.

blocks.title: Explain
blocks.text: With four independent instructions and three one-cycle stages, ideal completion is 3+4−1=6 cycles; serial non-overlap takes 4×3=12.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Data dependencies, branching and resource conflicts can stall or flush a pipeline. Throughput benefits need ideal assumptions, not automatic latency reductions.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the mechanism
blocks.text: 2+3−1=4 cycles; serial baseline 2×3=6 cycles. The second task starts stage one while first advances to stage two.

blocks.title: Explain the mechanism
blocks.text: 4+5−1=8 cycles, compared with 4×5=20 serial stage cycles. Assumes equal one-cycle stages, no resource conflicts or stalls.
